title: How to Repair a Garbage Disposer: Jam Clearing, Allen Wrench Access, and Torque Techniques
summary: This Old House demonstrates diagnosing and repairing a jammed garbage disposer. The video introduces disposer anatomy (flange, locking mechanism, splash guard), explains how waste travels into the disposer and how the dishwasher discharges into it, and then shows practical steps to clear a jam. When the motor hums due to an obstruction, the host uses the included Allen wrench to manually rotate the impeller, removes visible foreign objects with needle-nose pliers if needed, and, for higher torque, applies lever-based tools such as broomsticks and a pro wrench that can be fed through the splash guard to seat on the deck. After freeing the jam, the unit is tested to confirm smooth operation. The guidance emphasizes methodical diagnosis and controlled tool use rather than generic, off-camera procedures.

sections.title: Disposer anatomy and normal operation
sections.description: The presenter identifies the parts that connect the disposer to the sink: the flange, a locking connection underneath, and the splash guard that keeps water from splashing up. The video explains where the water and food enter, notes that the dishwasher discharges into the disposer, and describes how the cutter wheel and side teeth break up food before it is pushed toward the discharge path, driven by a motor when the unit is turned on.

sections.title: Overload and jam diagnosis; initial clearing with Allen wrench
sections.description: The host explains that excessive material or a foreign object can bind the cutter wheel, causing the motor to hum and trip an overload protection switch. The bottom access for the shaft is shown, and the included Allen wrench is used to turn the impeller manually in an attempt to clear the obstruction. If a fork or other object is visible, it can be removed with needle-nose pliers. If more torque is needed, the narrator describes progressing to higher-torque methods.

sections.title: Applying higher torque and alternative tools
sections.description: When manual rotation with the Allen wrench isn’t sufficient, the video demonstrates increasing torque using improvised tools such as opposing broomsticks to rotate the wheel and a professional wrench that can be fed down through the splash guard to sit on the deck for extra leverage.

sections.title: Test and confirmation
sections.description: After clearing the jam, the host tests the disposer again and confirms a proper, unobstructed operation.

featured_techniques.technique: Manual rotation of the disposer impeller with the included Allen wrench
Removing a foreign object with needle-nose pliers after inspection
Using broomsticks as levers to apply high torque
Using a pro wrench that seats through the splash guard for extra torque
